preconditions.description: The number of test cases T is an integer between 1 and 50,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(n, int) and 1 <= n <= 500000 for n in test_case_ns)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the number of vertices n is an integer between 1 and 500,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(edges) == n - 1 and all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in edges) for edges, n in zip(test_case_edges, test_case_ns))
preconditions.description: Each test case provides exactly n-1 edges connecting vertices within the range [1, n].

preconditions.expression: all(len(colors) == n and all(c in 'WN' for c in colors) for colors, n in zip(test_case_colors, test_case_ns))
preconditions.description: Each test case provides a color string of length n containing only 'W' (white) and 'N' (uncolored).

preconditions.expression: all('N' in colors for colors in test_case_colors)
preconditions.description: Each test case guarantees at least one uncolored vertex ('N').

preconditions.expression: all(not has_white_path_3(colors, edges) for colors, edges in zip(test_case_colors, test_case_edges))
preconditions.description: Each test case guarantees no path of three white vertices exists initially.
The sum of n across all test cases is at most 500,000.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly T lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(line in ['White', 'Draw', 'Black'] for line in stdout_lines)
postconditions.description: Each output line is exactly 'White', 'Draw', or 'Black'.

postconditions.expression: all(result_is_correct(stdout_lines[i], test_case_edges[i], test_case_colors[i]) for i in range(T))
postconditions.description: For each test case i, the output line correctly identifies the game outcome (White wins, Draw, or Black wins) assuming optimal play from both sides, where White wins if they can force a 3-vertex path, Black wins if they can force a 3-vertex path, and Draw if neither can force a win.
